title: James Webb Space Telescope (JWST): Deep Field Discoveries
executive_summary: Launched on December 25, 2021, the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is the premier space observatory, operating at infrared wavelengths to view early universe galaxies, exoplanet atmospheres, and stellar nurseries.
image_caption: Model of the James Webb Space Telescope displaying its 6.5-meter gold-coated primary mirror.

key_sections.title: Infrared Vision at Lagrange Point 2
key_sections.content: JWST orbits the Earth-Sun L2 point ~1.5 million km from Earth, protected by a 5-layer tennis-court-sized sunshield cooled to -233 °C (-388 °F) to detect faint infrared heat signals.

key_sections.title: First Light Galaxies and Early Universe
key_sections.content: JWST has uncovered luminous, unexpectedly mature galaxies formed just 300-400 million years after the Big Bang, challenging existing models of early galactic structure formation.

key_sections.title: Exoplanet Atmosphere Characterization
key_sections.content: JWST's NIRSpec and MIRI instruments have detected CO2, water vapor, and sulfur dioxide clouds in exoplanet atmospheres, including the famous TRAPPIST-1 system.
